nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $u \ge 2$, and let $a_1, \dots, a_{u-1} \in \{0, \dots, m\}$ with $a_1 \ne 0$. Writing $B_t = B_t^{(m+1)}$ for the blocks of the $(m+1)$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m+1)}$, the string $P = B_{u-1}^{a_{u-1}} \cdots B_2^{a_2} B_1^{a_1}$ has curling number $\mathcal{C}(P) \le m$.
nodes.title: Curling number of block words with small exponents

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $u \ge 1$, and let $a_1, \dots, a_{u-1} \in \{0, \dots, m+1\}$ with $a_i = m + 1$ for some $1 \le i \le u - 1$. Writing $B_t = B_t^{(m+1)}$ for the blocks of the $(m+1)$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m+1)}$, the string $P = B_{u-1}^{a_{u-1}} \cdots B_2^{a_2} B_1^{a_1}$ has curling number $\mathcal{C}(P) = m + 1$.
nodes.title: Curling number of block words with a maximal exponent

nodes.summary: The string $112112223$ has curling number $\mathcal{C}(112112223) = 1$.
nodes.title: Curling number of $112112223$

nodes.summary: The string $222322232223$ has curling number $\mathcal{C}(222322232223) = 3$.
nodes.title: Curling number of $222322232223$

nodes.summary: For strings $S$ and $T$ of natural numbers, if $T$ is a suffix of $S$, then $\mathcal{C}(T) \le \mathcal{C}(S)$.
nodes.title: The curling number is monotone under suffixes

nodes.summary: The empty string $\varepsilon$ has curling number $\mathcal{C}(\varepsilon) = 1$.
nodes.title: Curling number of the empty string

nodes.summary: The curling number $\mathcal{C}(S)$ of a finite string $S$ of natural numbers is the largest integer $k$ such that $S = X Y^k$ for some strings $X$ and $Y$ with $Y$ nonempty; for the empty string $\varepsilon$ it is $\mathcal{C}(\varepsilon) = 1$.
nodes.title: Curling number

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge m + 3$, and for $k \ge 1$ let $t(k, n)$ be the index $t$ such that the first occurrence of $n$ in the $k$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(k)}$ is the last element of the block $B_t^{(k)}$ of $A^{(k)}$. Then $m (m+1)^{t(m+1,n) - 2} \le t(m, n) \le (m+1)^{t(m+1,n) - 1} + 1$, and the second inequality is strict when $n = m + 3$.
nodes.title: Recursive estimate for the block index

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$, let $p$ be the position of the first occurrence of $n$ in the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m)}$, with $p = 0$ if $n$ does not occur. Then $t(m, n)$ is the least $t \ge 1$ such that the block length $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ equals $p$, so that when $n$ occurs, this first $n$ is the last element of the block $B_t^{(m)}$; if there is no such $t$, then $t(m, n) = 0$.
nodes.title: Block index of the first occurrence

nodes.summary: Let $M_7 = 4$ and $M_{k+1} = M_k (1 + 9 (k+1)^{1.59} / 2^k)$ for $k \ge 7$. Then for all $m \ge 1$ and $u \ge 7$, the block lengths $\beta^{(m)}(u)$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m)}$ satisfy $\beta^{(m)}(u) / (m+1)^{u-1} < M_u$.
nodes.title: Upper bound on block lengths

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $u \ge 2$. Write $\beta^{(m+1)}(u)$ for the length of the block $B_u^{(m+1)}$ of the $(m+1)$th order Gijswijt sequence, and $\tau^{(m)}(t)$ for the length of $T_t^{(m)} = S_1^{(m)} \cdots S_{t-1}^{(m)}$, the concatenation of the first $t - 1$ glue strings of order $m$. Then $\tau^{(m)}(m (m+1)^{u-2}) \le \beta^{(m+1)}(u) \le \tau^{(m)}((m+1)^{u-1} + 1)$, and the second inequality is strict when…
nodes.title: Bounds on the block lengths of order $m+1$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m$, the first block length $\beta^{(m)}(1)$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence equals $1$.
nodes.title: The first block has length one

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $A^{(m)}(k)$ for the $k$th term of the $m$th order sequence. The block lengths $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ are defined by $\beta^{(m)}(0) = 0$, $\beta^{(m)}(1) = 1$ and, for $t \ge 1$, $\beta^{(m)}(t+1)$ is the least $k > (m+1)\,\beta^{(m)}(t)$ with $A^{(m)}(k+1) = m$, or $0$ if there is no such $k$.
nodes.title: Block lengths of the higher-order Gijswijt sequences

nodes.summary: For every $m \ge 1$, the first block $B_1^{(m)}$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence is the one-term string $m$.
nodes.title: The first block

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $t \ge 2$, and consider the block $B_t^{(m)}$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence. Every maximal run of consecutive terms equal to $m$ in $B_t^{(m)}$ has length exactly $m + 1$, and the term right after the run exists and equals $m + 1$.
nodes.title: Runs of the smallest term in a block

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m$ and every sequence of exponents $a_1, a_2, \ldots$, the block word $B_{u-1}^{a_{u-1}} \cdots B_1^{a_1}$ of order $m$ with $u = 1$, where $B_i$ is the $i$th block of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence, is a product of no blocks and hence the empty string.
nodes.title: The empty block word

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $u$ and exponents $a_1, a_2, \ldots$, the block word of order $m$ is the concatenation $B_{u-1}^{a_{u-1}} \cdots B_2^{a_2} B_1^{a_1}$, where $B_i = B_i^{(m)}$ is the $i$th block of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence and $B_i^{a_i}$ is $a_i$ copies of $B_i$ in a row. Only $a_1, \ldots, a_{u-1}$ are used, and the word is empty when $u \le 1$.
nodes.title: Block words

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $t$, the block $B_t^{(m)}$ is the prefix of length $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m)}$, where $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ is the $t$th block length.
nodes.title: Gijswijt blocks

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le m \le n$, and write $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ for the length of the block $B_t^{(m)}$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m)}$. Then there is a $t \ge 1$ such that $A^{(m)}(\beta^{(m)}(t)) = n$ and $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ is the position of the first occurrence of $n$ in $A^{(m)}$; that is, the first $n$ in $A^{(m)}$ is the last term of the block $B_t^{(m)}$.
nodes.title: First occurrences end blocks

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 4$ there is a real number $\alpha$ with $n - 2 < \alpha < n - 1$ such that the first occurrence of $n$ in Gijswijt's sequence is at position $2^{2^{3^{\cdot^{\cdot^{(n-2)^{\alpha}}}}}}$, a power tower whose bases are $2, 2, 3, \ldots, n-2$ from the bottom up and whose top exponent is $\alpha$; for $n = 4$ it is $2^{2^{\alpha}}$.
nodes.title: Van de Pol's tower formula for first occurrences

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$, the first occurrence of $n$ in the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m)}$ is the least position $k \ge 1$ with $A^{(m)}(k) = n$, and it is $0$ if $n$ does not occur in $A^{(m)}$.
nodes.title: First occurrence of a value in a Gijswijt sequence

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge m + 1$. For $j \ge 1$ let $t(j, n)$ be the least $t \ge 1$ such that the block $B^{(j)}_t$ of the $j$th order Gijswijt sequence has length equal to the position of the first occurrence of $n$ in that sequence (this position is taken to be $0$ if $n$ does not occur), and $t(j, n) = 0$ if there is no such $t$. Then the concatenated glue string $T^{(m)}_{t(m,n)}$ equals the block…
nodes.title: Concatenated glue strings at first occurrences are blocks of the next order

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $u \ge 2$, and for exponents $a_1, \ldots, a_{u-1}$ let $W(a) = (B^{(m+1)}_{u-1})^{a_{u-1}} \cdots (B^{(m+1)}_1)^{a_1}$ be the word in the blocks of the $(m+1)$th order Gijswijt sequence. (a) If $t \ge 1$ and the concatenated glue string $T^{(m)}_t$ is a proper prefix of $B^{(m+1)}_u$, then $T^{(m)}_t = W(a)$ for some $a_1, \ldots, a_{u-1} \in \{0, \ldots, m\}$. (b) For all…
nodes.title: Concatenated glue strings inside a block of the next order

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$. A finite string $P$ of natural numbers is a prefix of the $(m+1)$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m+1)}$ with curling number $\mathcal{C}(P) \le m$ if and only if $P = T^{(m)}_t$ for some $t \ge 1$, where $T^{(m)}_t$ is the concatenated glue string.
nodes.title: Concatenated glue strings are the next-order prefixes with small curling number

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $t \ge 2$, write $\tau^{(m)}(t)$ for the length of the concatenated glue string $T^{(m)}_t$ and $\beta^{(m+1)}$ for the block lengths of the $(m+1)$th order Gijswijt sequence, and let $c$ be the least natural number with $t \le (m+1)^c$, that is, $c = \lceil \log_{m+1} t \rceil$. Then $\beta^{(m+1)}(c) \le \tau^{(m)}(t) \le \beta^{(m+1)}(c + 2)$.
nodes.title: Length estimates for concatenated glue strings

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m$, the concatenated glue string $T^{(m)}_1$ is the empty string.
nodes.title: The first concatenated glue string is empty

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $t \ge 2$. The element $m$ followed by the concatenated glue string $T^{(m)}_t$ is a suffix of the block $B^{(m)}_t$, and whenever $B^{(m)}_t = X\,T^{(m)}_t\,Y$ for strings $X$ and $Y$, the string $Y$ is empty; that is, $T^{(m)}_t$ occurs in $B^{(m)}_t$ only as a suffix.
nodes.title: Concatenated glue strings occur in a block only at its end

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $t$, the string $T^{(m)}_t$ is the concatenation $S^{(m)}_1 S^{(m)}_2 \cdots S^{(m)}_{t-1}$ of the glue strings of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence; it is empty when $t \le 1$.
nodes.title: Concatenated glue strings of a Gijswijt sequence

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $t$, the glue string $S^{(m)}_t$ is the block $B^{(m)}_{t+1}$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence with its first $(m+1)\,\beta^{(m)}(t)$ elements removed, where $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ is the length of the block $B^{(m)}_t$.
nodes.title: Glue strings of a Gijswijt sequence

nodes.summary: The first nine terms of Gijswijt's sequence $A^{(1)}$ are $1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3$.
nodes.title: First terms of Gijswijt's sequence

nodes.summary: The first eight terms of the second-order sequence $A^{(2)}$ are $2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 3$.
nodes.title: Initial terms of the second-order Gijswijt sequence

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers. The list of the first $n$ terms of the $m$th order sequence $A^{(m)}$ is defined by recursion on $n$: for $n = 0$ it is the empty list, and the list for $n + 1$ is the list $P$ for $n$ followed by the term $\max(m, \mathcal{C}(P))$, where $\mathcal{C}(P)$ is the curling number of $P$ (the largest $k$ with $P = XY^k$ for strings $X$, $Y$ with $Y$ nonempty, and $1$ for the empty…
nodes.title: Prefixes of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $u \ge 1$, and write $B_t$ for the block $B_t^{(m+1)}$ of the $(m+1)$th order Gijswijt sequence. A string $P$ is a proper prefix of $B_u$ (a prefix strictly shorter than $B_u$) with curling number $\mathcal{C}(P) \le m + 1$ if and only if $P = B_{u-1}^{a_{u-1}} \cdots B_2^{a_2} B_1^{a_1}$ for some natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_{u-1} \le m + 1$, where $B_t^{a}$ denotes $a$ copies of $B_t$…
nodes.title: Proper prefixes of a block with curling number at most $m + 1$

nodes.summary: For $k \ge 1$, $A^{(m)}(k)$ is the $k$th term of the $m$th order sequence $A^{(m)}$, that is, the last entry of the list of its first $k$ terms. For $k = 0$ the value is $0$ by convention.
nodes.title: Terms of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
